observation.visible_scene: A macro close-up of a dark, pointed metal blade (tip pointing left) held against a pale surface with a rounded, beaded/hexagonal texture (foam- or stipple-like). A row of light rounded protrusions runs along the top edge of the blade, and a shadowed region of the same beaded texture lies below the blade edge. The blade body extends off-frame to the right throughout.
visible_changes: The apparent orientation of the blade shifts from a diagonal (tip low-center, edge rising to the upper-right) in the early frames to nearly horizontal in the later frames.
The blade tip drifts leftward within the frame, from roughly the horizontal center in the first frames to the far-left edge in the final frames.

The pale beaded material above the blade edge becomes more clearly resolved as a discrete row of rounded bumps as the clip progresses, while a darker beaded/shadowed zone grows visible beneath the blade.
The background texture and the soft shadow above the blade move relative to the frame, indicating a change in viewpoint or object position.
No clear start or end of an action is present; the blade-material contact line is visible from the first to the last sampled frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the blade is being driven into, slicing, or merely resting against the textured material.
Whether the apparent rotation/leftward drift is produced by camera movement, by the blade being repositioned, or by both.
What lies beyond the right edge of the frame (handle, full blade, the operator).
Whether the beaded texture is a single object or two surfaces sandwiching the blade.
uncertain_details: The material identity of the pale beaded surface (foam, plaster, 3D-printed infill, etc.) cannot be confirmed from the images.
The cause of the orientation change (camera pan/tilt vs. physical blade rotation) is not disambiguated by background evidence alone.
Some frames are motion-blurred, so exact contact geometry between blade edge and material is approximate.
